title: Retire the execution packages from ticks
description:
Delete the execution machinery from ticks. Until this lands, "extracted" means
"copied", and two codebases drift.

Retire from ticks `internal/herd/`, once ticfac drives runs:
- `client/`, `herdtest/`, `gitcmd/` — lifted in tick 579.
- `spawn/`, `wait/`, `reconcile/`, `cleanup/`, `state/` (~7800 lines) — REPLACED
  rather than lifted: ticfac's reconciler already owns waves, adoption,
  disposition and cleanup, and its JobHandle plus run-state already carry what
  `state.Manifest` carried.
- `notify/`, `paint/`, `collect/` — decide per package. Paint needs exactly ONE
  tracker fact (a status lookup by tick id, paint.go:357) and collect needs ONE
  path predicate (the `.tick/` boundary check, collect.go:219); behind a
  callback each, both become execution-only and move.

STAYS in ticks, by design:
- `relay/` — the durable operator question. Heavily wired into operator.Engine,
  roughly fifteen call sites. This is tracker domain and must not move.
- `dashboard/` — it exists to JOIN tracker state with run state (WaveRow and
  TickRow are built from tick.Tick and state.Manifest in one function,
  snapshot.go:323,361). There is no seam inside that type. It becomes a CONSUMER
  of ticfac rather than a part of it, which means it needs a supported way to
  read run state — the `.ticfac/` records, or the run feed in backlog tick n0r.

Also close the ten direct `.tick/` crossings the herd packages hold today
(state.go:29,133,189,207; config/types.go:9; config/load.go:132;
paint.go:357; dashboard/snapshot.go:151; dashboard/fswatch.go:82,139;
collect.go:219) — each either moves with its package or becomes a callback.

Do this LAST among the implementation ticks. Deleting before ticfac genuinely
drives a run leaves no way back.
acceptance_criteria: ticks' internal/herd contains only relay and dashboard plus what they need; the execution packages are deleted, not duplicated; the ten direct .tick/ reads in the retired packages are gone or became callbacks; the dashboard reads run state through a supported interface rather than a lifted internal type; ticks builds and its tests pass; ticfac's gate is green; a real ticks epic still runs end to end through ticfac.
